Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Conversation, family & daily routines · Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

tiny adjective

also very small, teeny

classical

Phaedr. 5.3.3: volucris parvulae
Hor. S. 1.1.33: parvola … formīca (Lewis & Short)

parvulus, parvula, parvulum

adjective

tiny, very small

Also spelled parvolus. Of age too: ā parvulō, from a tiny child (Ter. And. 1.1.8, Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • pusillus, pusilla, pusillum — very little, wee

    adjective · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 5.2.2: quasi pusillam Rōmam; Plaut. Truc. 4.4.15: mūs (Lewis & Short)

    Often a little scornful: petty.

  • minūtus, minūta, minūtum — minute, tiny

    adjective · also used · classical · Varr. RR 1.12.2: animālia quaedam minūta

  • perparvus, perparva, perparvum — very small

    adjective · also used · classical · Lucr. 3.216 (Lewis & Short); Cic. Leg. 1.52 (Lewis & Short)

Examples

  • pūnctum volucris parvulae voluistī morte ulcīscī

    you wanted to pay back a tiny fly’s sting with deathPhaedr. 5.3.3–4

  • crēscunt animālia quaedam minūta, quae nōn possunt oculī cōnsequī

    certain tiny creatures breed there, too small for the eye to seeVarr. RR 1.12.2

  • habuimus in Cūmānō quasi pusillam Rōmam

    we had a sort of tiny Rome at the house at CumaeCic. Att. 5.2.2

See also big, too small, small.
